claim: The configuration recorder stores configuration changes of the in-scope resource types as configuration items; it is either customer managed (you set the resource types, by default all supported resources in the Region) or service-linked (the linked service sets the scope).
question: What does the AWS Config configuration recorder do, and what kinds are there?

values.display: stores the configuration changes to the resource types in scope
There are two types of configuration recorders.

evidence.quote: The *configuration recorder* stores the configuration changes to the resource types in scope as configuration items.

| Customer managed configuration recorder | A configuration recorder that you managed. The resource types in scope are set by you. By default, a customer managed configuration recorder records all supported resources in the AWS Region where AWS Config is running. |
| Service-linked configuration recorder | A configuration recorder that is linked to a specific AWS service. The resource types in scope are set by the linked service. |

claim: AWS Config rule triggers are configuration changes (evaluate when an in-scope resource changes), periodic (evaluate at a frequency you choose) or hybrid (both).
question: When does an AWS Config rule run?

values.display: in response to configuration changes or periodically
at a frequency that you choose
Some rules have both configuration change and periodic triggers.

evidence.quote: | Periodic | AWS Config runs evaluations for the rule at a frequency that you choose; for example, every 24 hours. |

| Hybrid | Some rules have both configuration change and periodic triggers. For these rules, AWS Config evaluates your resources when it detects a configuration change and also at the frequency that you specify.  |
Depending on the rule, AWS Config will evaluate your resources either in response to configuration changes or periodically.

claim: AWS Config rules have two evaluation modes: proactive evaluates resources before they are deployed, and detective evaluates resources that are already deployed; proactive rules do not remediate noncompliant resources or prevent them from being deployed.
question: Does an AWS Config proactive rule block a noncompliant deployment?

values.display: There are two evaluation modes for AWS Config rules.
evaluate resources that have already been deployed
Proactive rules do not remediate resources

evidence.quote: There are two evaluation modes for AWS Config rules.
| Detective | Use detective evaluation to evaluate resources that have already been deployed. This allows you to evaluate the configuration settings of your existing resources. |
Proactive rules do not remediate resources that are flagged as NON\_COMPLIANT or prevent them from being deployed.

note: d086, d087. The proactive row ('evaluate resources before they have been deployed') is a long table row with links; the voter sees it in context.

claim: AWS Config remediates noncompliant resources by using AWS Systems Manager Automation documents, either managed automation documents that AWS Config provides or custom ones you associate with rules; each remediation action can be manual or automatic.
question: How does AWS Config fix a noncompliant resource?

values.display: AWS Systems Manager Automation documents
a set of managed automation documents with remediation actions
you can either choose manual or automatic remediation

evidence.quote: AWS Config applies remediation using AWS Systems Manager Automation documents.
AWS Config provides a set of managed automation documents with remediation actions. You can also create and associate custom automation documents with AWS Config rules.
With all remediation actions, you can either choose manual or automatic remediation.

claim: If a resource is still noncompliant after auto remediation, you can set the rule to retry; retries run only when remediation fails, within the time period you set, and each run of the remediation script has a cost.
question: What happens if AWS Config auto remediation does not fix the resource the first time?

values.display: you can set the rule to try auto remediation again
There are costs associated with running a remediation script multiple times.

evidence.quote: If a resource is still noncompliant after auto remediation, you can set the rule to try auto remediation again.
There are costs associated with running a remediation script multiple times. Retries only occur if remediation fails and work within the specified time period; for example, 5 retries in 300 seconds.

claim: An AWS Config aggregator collects configuration and compliance data from multiple accounts and Regions, from a single account across Regions, or from an organization in AWS Organizations and all its accounts that have AWS Config enabled.
question: From which sources can an AWS Config aggregator collect data?

values.display: Multiple accounts and multiple AWS Regions.
An organization in AWS Organizations and all the accounts in that organization which have AWS Config enabled.

qualifiers.condition: source accounts must have AWS Config enabled

evidence.quote: Multiple accounts and multiple AWS Regions.
An organization in AWS Organizations and all the accounts in that organization which have AWS Config enabled.

claim: AWS Config advanced queries use a subset of SQL SELECT syntax to query the current configuration state of resources without service-specific describe calls, and with an aggregator the same queries run from a central account across multiple accounts and Regions.
question: How do you list, for example, all S3 buckets with versioning disabled across many accounts?

values.display: a subset of structured query language (SQL)
use configuration aggregators to run the same queries from a central account

qualifiers.scope: per account and Region, or per aggregator

evidence.quote: You can use configuration aggregators to run the same queries from a central account across multiple accounts and AWS Regions.
AWS Config uses a subset of structured query language (SQL) `SELECT` syntax to perform property-based queries and aggregations on the current configuration item (CI) data.

claim: AWS Config organizational rules let you centrally create, update and delete rules across all accounts, and from the management account you can make them not modifiable by member accounts; organizational rules can be created only with the API or CLI, not in the console.
question: How do you deploy AWS Config rules to every account so members cannot change them?

values.display: Centrally create, update, and delete AWS Config rules across all accounts
not modifiable by your organization’s member accounts
Organizational rules can only be created using the API or CLI.

evidence.quote: Organizational rules can only be created using the API or CLI. This operation is not supported in the AWS Config console.
Centrally create, update, and delete AWS Config rules across all accounts in your organization.
Use the APIs from the management account in AWS Organizations to enforce governance by ensuring that the underlying AWS Config rules are not modifiable by your organization’s member accounts.

claim: AWS Config can stream configuration changes and notifications to an Amazon SNS topic, including configuration item changes and the compliance state of resources against your rules; the configuration recorder and delivery channel must be set up first.
question: How do you get an email when a resource configuration or its compliance state changes in AWS Config?

values.display: stream configuration changes and notifications to an Amazon SNS topic
Compliance state of your resources and whether they are compliant with your rules.

qualifiers.condition: configuration recorder and delivery channel set up

evidence.quote: You can configure AWS Config to stream configuration changes and notifications to an Amazon SNS topic.
Compliance state of your resources and whether they are compliant with your rules.
Before AWS Config can send notifications to an Amazon SNS topic, you must first set up the configuration recorder and the delivery channel.
